content.text:
**Candidate06 resolves the queued-reset blocker and isolates ordinary subscriber failures, but fault isolation still has a reproducible error-reporting hole.** I found no concrete new scheduler regression in the inspected paths.

- **Queued reset:** [clock_scheduler.c:285](/home/andy/projects/monome-runtime-candidates/midi-clock-boundary-06/norns/matron/src/clocks/clock_scheduler.c:285) rearms waiting/queued syncs under the same mutex used by [claim_resume:319](/home/andy/projects/monome-runtime-candidates/midi-clock-boundary-06/norns/matron/src/clocks/clock_scheduler.c:319). Claiming clears `queued`; a subsequent reset leaves that running coroutine alone, and its next sync rebases through the epoch check at line202. [events.c:215](/home/andy/projects/monome-runtime-candidates/midi-clock-boundary-06/norns/matron/src/events.c:215) enters Lua after claiming and releasing the scheduler lock. Scheduler polling only publishes events—no scheduler-thread Lua reentry. Cancellation clears queued state; sleep claims deliberately survive epoch changes.

- **Remaining fault-isolation defect:** [clock.lua:221](/home/andy/projects/monome-runtime-candidates/midi-clock-boundary-06/norns/lua/core/clock.lua:221) executes `tostring(err)` outside protection. I reproduced a callback throwing `error(setmetatable({}, {__tostring=function() error("formatting failed") end}))` against the installed06 Lua file: the shared resume failed, **no F8 or healthy callback ran**, no subscription diagnostic appeared, and the next resume reported `cannot resume dead coroutine`. The same formatter handles `on_error` failures. Protect diagnostic conversion with a safe fallback and cover both entry paths. This is an uncommon but concrete remaining instance of the original blocker.

- **Positive evidence:** I reran all ten supplied Lua cases successfully, including yielding callbacks, failing handlers, and clear-subscriptions-then-fail. [Recorded native results](/home/andy/projects/monome-emulator-midi-clock/artifacts/midi-clock/boundary-fixes-native-01.json:1) show the04 queued-reset failure and06 queued-reset, fault-isolation, and normal-output passes in D/R. These establish the ordinary paths; they do not cover the formatter failure.

- **Mosaic follow-up:** [midi_output_transport.lua:37](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/clock/midi_output_transport.lua:37) still supplies no `on_error` cleanup. Disabling its subscription can leave transport state and the intermediate coroutine active; wire failure into cancellation and appropriate note-release cleanup. Forwarding, multiport/remapping, lifecycle, and gate/wrap/tempo validation remain outstanding. The [06 Mosaic results](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-runs/midi-boundary-regressions-02.json:1) were still marked running when inspected; earlier04 results do not establish06 completion.

**CONFIDENCE: High.** A protected formatter plus passing callback/handler error-object regressions would close the remaining native finding; I did not rerun native processes or establish full musical acceptance.
